MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Sex: Female
Ethnicity: White European
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Cystic fibrosis carrier testing requested for pregnant woman with family history of CF. Known familial CFTR pathogenic variant c.1521_1523delCTT p.(Phe508del) identified in affected family member.

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Patient is currently pregnant and has requested carrier screening due to family history of cystic fibrosis. A family member has been diagnosed with CF and carries the c.1521_1523delCTT p.(Phe508del) pathogenic variant in the CFTR gene.

TEST METHODOLOGY
CF-Screen Panel
Targeted PCR-based screening for common pathogenic variants in the CFTR gene
Panel detects 50 variants representing approximately 88% of CF-causing variants in the Caucasian population
Includes specific testing for the known familial variant c.1521_1523delCTT p.(Phe508del)
Methodology: Allele-specific PCR with fluorescent detection
Analytical sensitivity: >99% for variants included in panel

RESULTS
Gene: CFTR (NM_000492.4)
Result: NEGATIVE - No pathogenic variants detected

Variants Tested: 50 common CFTR pathogenic variants including:
- c.1521_1523delCTT p.(Phe508del) - NOT DETECTED
- c.1652G>A p.(Gly551Asp) - NOT DETECTED
- c.1624G>T p.(Gly542*) - NOT DETECTED
- c.489+1G>T - NOT DETECTED
[Additional variants tested as per CF-Screen panel]

SUMMARY
No pathogenic variants were detected in this CFTR carrier screen. The known familial variant c.1521_1523delCTT p.(Phe508del) was specifically tested and not detected in this patient.

Based on the negative result and the patient's White European ethnicity, the residual carrier risk is reduced from the population risk of approximately 1/25 to approximately 1/802.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
This negative result significantly reduces but does not eliminate the patient's risk of being a CF carrier. Given the negative carrier screen in this patient and assuming the partner is not a known CF carrier, prenatal testing for cystic fibrosis is not indicated based on current guidelines.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results and their implications for the current pregnancy
2. Partner carrier screening may be considered based on ethnicity and family history
3. Carrier testing is available for other adult family members who may be at risk
4. Genetic counseling is recommended prior to testing family members to discuss benefits, risks, and limitations of carrier screening

TECHNICAL NOTES AND LIMITATIONS
- This test screens for 50 common CFTR pathogenic variants and detects approximately 88% of CF-causing variants in individuals of Caucasian ancestry
- Detection rates vary by ethnicity: Ashkenazi Jewish (94%), Hispanic (72%), African American (65%), Asian (49%)
- This test does not detect all CFTR variants; therefore, a negative result does not rule out carrier status
- Rare variants, deep intronic variants, and large deletions/duplications may not be detected by this methodology
- Full CFTR gene sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis is available if clinically indicated

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
CAP: [redacted ID] | CLIA: [redacted ID]
